newsitem.title: USA: Sears, Roebuck sees 5,000 stores by year 2000.
newsitem.headline: Sears, Roebuck sees 5,000 stores by year 2000.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Friday it expects to have about 5,000 stores by the year 2000, almost twice its current total.
"We are optimistic that our current momentum can carry us to the 5,000 level by the year 2000," said Ron Culp, Sears vice president of public affairs, in a telephone interview.
Sears, the second largest retailer in the United States, has more than 2,700 stores. That includes 808 department stores in malls and more than 1,900 free-standing or "off-the-mall" stores.

These off-the-mall specialty stores, which have been driving Sears sales, include 104 HomeLife home furnishings stores, 115 Sears Hardware stores, and 1,750 Parts America auto parts stores and Western Auto auto parts and vehicle repair stores.
Sears has said it will continue its strategy of generating sales by expanding its specialty retail stores through acquisition and by building stores.
"Growth by the turn the century will come predominately from off-the-mall stores," Culp said, adding that the plan is to have about 860 mall stores and over 4,000 off-the-mall units.

Sears is in the process of completing a $415 million acquisition of California-based Orchard Supply Hardware Stores Corp. That will give the retailer 61 medium-sized hardware stores in California, a new market for the retailer. Orchard Supply plans call for a total of 150 stores in California over the next several years.
By year end, Sears expects to have a total of 450 Sears dealer stores, independently owned stores mostly in rural areas, which sell appliances, electronics, and batteries.
Sears' funding for expansion "traditionally comes from cash flow rather than from debt flow," Culp said.
Its "big retailing segment is virtually debt free, a rare status among the big retailers," said Tom Tashjian, retail analyst at Montgomery Securities, in a recent report.
"Sears is in very strong financial shape as all of its debt is carried by the credit card segment and more than offset by the backing of its accounts receivable portfolio, the report said.

Sears reported that total sales for the first 30 weeks of the year rose to $20.21 billion, a level which ranks it as second largest U.S. retailer. Wal-Mart Stores Inc with sales for the 30 weeks of $56.36 billion ranks as the largest.
